full_title: Hazard modeling, impact estimation, climate storylines for event catalogue on drought and flood disasters in the Eastern Africa
project_blurb:
A new composite-risk initiative that is transforming drought and
flood modelling across Eastern Africa. It pairs ensemble forecasts with concise climate storylines to reveal how climate, conflict, and displacement pressures overlap. The resulting hazard-impact datasets give governments and humanitarian partners a sharper basis for impact-based forecasting, anticipatory action, and loss-and-damage assessment. Led by ICPAC, the project will feed these insights into early-warning triggers and response planning across East Africa.

full_title: Geoguard - Geospatial Dashboards for Climate Assessment and Early Warning
project_blurb:
Geoguard is a geospatial crisis-forecasting platform that brings
together environmental, conflict, and social data to surface patterns linked to emerging climate-security risks. Piloted across Central Africa, West Africa, and the Middle East, its methodology has been applied in 29 countries. With CRAF’d support, the platform is strengthening its data infrastructure and expanding collaboration on transboundary risks. Developed by the Innovation Cell of the United Nations Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA), Geoguard supports preventive efforts through geospatial analysis.

full_title: Maintaining & Improving ACLED's Core Operations, Accessibility, and Interoperability
project_blurb:
With a new two-year CRAF’d grant (2024-2026), ACLED is expanding its reach, sharpening its tools, and delivering conflict
insights when they matter most. ACLED is the world’s leading
source of high-quality, real-time data and analysis on political violence and protest, powering earlier, faster, and more targeted crisis action. Its trusted, evidence-based insights serve policymakers, humanitarian practitioners, journalists, academics, and the
wider public. With global coverage, ACLED has documented more
than 1.9 million conflict events from sources in over 100 languages, grounded in more than 60 partnerships and long standing
relationships with local actors across the crisis data ecosystem.
The CRAF’d-ACLED partnership has already delivered tangible
results, reinforcing ACLED’s role as a cornerstone of the crisis
data ecosystem. Between 2022 and 2024, ACLED nearly doubled
its registered users to over 67,000, expanded its network to more
than 60 partners, and introduced or refined 5 analytical tools now
embedded in decision-making processes and program planning to
better anticipate, prevent, and respond to crises.

full_title: Kente Threads: Weaving leadership from displacement data
project_blurb:
A participatory data initiative rooted in local leadership,
including HERDATA, is set to strengthen crisis response
and resilience by elevating displaced women’s leadership. Led by the Feminist Humanitarian Network
with local partners, the project will reach over 100,000
women in displacement settings.

project_label: Korbel: Women's Mobilization Within Armed Groups
full_title: Women’s Mobilization Within Armed Groups During and After War
project_blurb:
A first-of-its-kind global dataset on women’s roles
in non-state armed groups is set to enhance peacebuilding across 500 women’s wings of non-state
armed groups. Led by the University of Denver in
collaboration with research partners, the project will
inform programming in conflict-affected settings.

full_title: Global harmonized data on internal displacement to inform prevention, response and solutions
project_blurb: The IDMC is reshaping how displacement data drives crisis action. By applying AI, automated pipelines, and a worldwide monitoring network, it harmonizes the leading datasets on internal displacement, now affecting more than 83 million people, to deliver timely, disaggregated insights. IDMC equips humanitarian and development actors with the evidence needed for faster, more targeted, and dignified support.

full_title: Transformative Outcomes: Leveraging Crisis Data in conflict
project_blurb:
Disaggregated data made accessible through an interactive platform and standardized analysis will support
more informed, real-time assistance for at least 20
million people in crisis settings. The project is led by
UN Women and backed by a broad coalition of six
national NGO partners.

full_title: INFORM WARNING - An open system to aggregate and present quantified, multi-hazard information to support crisis preparedness and anticipatory action
project_blurb: INFORM Warning is setting a new benchmark for global risk anticipation. Developed by a global consortium of over 35 partners, INFORM Warning will be a state-of-the-art global risk monitoring tool for anticipating complex risks up to a year in advance. As part of the INFORM product family, it complements existing tools by linking baseline risk metrics to actionable foresight. INFORM Warning beyond traditional methods by integrating new multi-hazard information from diverse sources. The tool’s distinctive approach will provide valuable insights into forecasts, scenarios, and potential crisis-triggering events. Hosted by United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Crisis Bureau, the platform is being scaled globally with support from CRAF’d.

full_title: Conflict-climate-displacement & vulnerability data in Africa and MENA
project_blurb:
A new generation risk data initiative is shining a light on where
climate, conflict, and displacement risks collide across sub-Saharan Africa, North Africa, and the Middle East (MENA). By integrating these drivers into one analytical stream, it delivers actionable insights tailored to conflict-affected and climate-vulnerable populations, filling critical gaps and enabling anticipatory action. Led by the Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre, together with the Netherlands Red Cross’ 510 Initiative and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the risk data supports more informed and anticipatory decision-making across the humanitarian system.

full_title: Progressive Representation of Internal Migration and Risk Intelligence (PRIMARI)
project_blurb: PRIMARI sets a new benchmark for displacement insight. Delivered through IOM’s public Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) API, the open, sub-national dataset merges mobility-tracking and flow-monitoring data from up to 90 countries. Its harmonized feeds let responders track movements in near-real time, map emerging risks, and direct assistance faster. Backed by CRAF’d, IOM’s Global Data Institute is positioning PRIMARI as the humanitarian sector’s core data backbone.

full_title: Gender Understanding and Analysis for Response to Disasters
project_blurb:
Innovative real-time data and tools will identify at-risk
populations within 48 hours of disasters, enabling
faster and more equitable response. Led by IFRC with
a broad coalition of eight partners, the project could
improve assistance for up to 100 million people.

full_title: Strengthening the CRAF’d Data Ecosystem for More Effective Crisis Action
project_blurb:
With this project, CRAF’d and its partners help better connect
stakeholders across the crisis data ecosystem. Conferences,
research and other initiatives supported by this project are designed to bring data providers, practitioners, and policy experts together. NORCAP acts as the manager for the project and collaborates closely with CRAF’d and its partners to enable ecosystem activities.

full_title: VIEWS-PIN: People in Need
project_blurb:
VIEWS-PIN is breaking new ground in forecasting conflict-driven
humanitarian needs. It blends curated, high-resolution conflict and climate data with advanced machine learning to deliver sub-national forecasts up to 36 months in advance. Available via an open dashboard, these forecasts inform planning for food insecurity, displacement, and political violence in fragile settings. Developed by the PRIO and Uppsala University, VIEWS-PIN brings over 60 years of conflict research into the next generation of early warning systems.

full_title: Rapid Assessment Data: Preventing conflict-related sexual violence
project_blurb:
Cutting-edge AI-powered data on conflict-related sexual
violence will expand coverage, accelerate reporting,
and inform more than $15 million in protection efforts.
Piloted in six conflict-affected countries, the project is
led by Office of the United Nations High Commissioner
for Human Rights with a view to broader scale-up

full_title: Environmental Early Action and Risk Tracking Hub (EEARTH)
project_blurb:
The Environmental Early Action and Risk Tracking Hub (eEARTH)
is breaking new ground in how we anticipate climate-driven conflict. Piloted in Somalia and South Sudan, it equips decision-makers with tailored intelligence to prevent crises before they escalate. Developed by the International Crisis Group, the leading conflict prevention organization grounded in field research, eEARTH transforms data into timely, anticipatory action.

full_title: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED)
project_blurb: N/A

full_title: Risk Anticipation Data Hub
project_blurb: A next-generation platform brings more than 15,000 crisis indicators into one open, AI-enabled space, making risk data faster, smarter, and easier to act on. Drawing from over 20 public sources, it pairs real-time analytics with a conversational AI assistant so users can query risks in plain language, track emerging threats, and pull insights directly into their own systems through an open API, supporting over 7,500 practitioners across the humanitarian, development, and peace fields. The Data Hub is being developed by United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Crisis Bureau to help partners to better crisis anticipation, prevention, and response.

full_title: Women’s Empowerment in Peace Processes
project_blurb:
A new multi-decade dataset tracking women’s roles
in peace processes is set to improve inclusive peacebuilding worldwide. Led by Peace Research Institute
Oslo (PRIO) with academic partners, the project will
share open data and insights that could benefit 20
million people.

full_title: CLIFDEW-GRID: Early Warning Grid-Based Risk Modelling of Climate Induced Forced Displacement
project_blurb: CLIFDEW-GRID is redefining how we understand climate-induced displacement. By shifting from national averages to a granular, grid-level view, this pioneering model captures where and how displacement risks are rising across West and East Africa. Drawing on cutting-edge analytics, the initiative offers a powerful tool to anticipate future hotspots and enable faster, more targeted crisis action. Developed by UNHCR and the University of California, Irvine, CLIFDEW-GRID helps turn data into early action.

With CRAF’d funding, ACLED continues providing real-time, geo-coded and disaggregated conflict data worldwide and enables its 40,000 users to generate insights that feed directly into evidence-based policymaking and decision-making, strategic planning, and effective programming around the world.
